column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, update v131072)

# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive; project Owl, the Tears of the Kingdom engine's file layout), SDK 22.2.8 built for the Switch 2 (Ounce), NVN2 (Ampere shaders); modules main + subsdk0 (movie) + sdk.
# Packed from a NUP container (scripts/pack_nup.py). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code).

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # In the NUP at hand three RomFS files begin with 12 KB of zeros (the container's SHA-256 of them matches, so they were so when it was packed; whether a retail copy has them is not known), so they cannot be decompressed. Served as stored, the fairy
# fountain model that uses the first never loaded and the OptimizeChangeBanc thread (main+0xf7a0) asked for it again ~22 times a second all session: one core, plus ~0.75 core of
# ParallelDecompThread decompressing the 2.4 MB model each time (Mac CPU 365%, iPad 400-460%). "Not found" fails the model the same way. Served as the game's own 1x1 flat normal map, the
# model loads once and both threads go idle (Mac CPU 412% -> 180%, frame p95 21.9 -> 18.8 ms). The Ganon stage bake is served as its neighbour cell's (not checked in game). A copy without the damage
# needs none of this: the host substitutes only a .zs file that is not a zstd stream (hle_fs.c img_serve)
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.

# nninitStartup asks SetHeapSize 0x18ce00000 (6.2 GB) with the 9 GB pool, as Mario Kart World. 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 8 GB heap region: a starting split, to be measured
# Memory savers for a 16 GB Mac, from kid-with-sword-remake (a758ea2d), which plays with them on such a Mac; not measured on this branch's host. GPU memory guard as before (the system's side too).
# Large block-compressed textures from the game files kept without their finest level on the GPU (nvn_mtl.m tex_soft): about three quarters of each such texture's GPU bytes, a little
# softer up close. 2D arrays stay whole: kid-with-sword's notes have the reflection probes' water under Kokiri Forest's canopy showing flat sky with them soft. DM_NVN_TEX_SOFT=0 turns it off
# A finalized texture's ID that no shader has read gets the dummy instead of its texture made again (nvn_mtl.m pool_skip_retired; upstream PR #1393: GPU allocated 11.4 GB against 13.2
# at the Kokiri Forest door on an older host). DM_NVN_POOL_SKIP_RETIRED=0 turns it off

# Colour render targets drawn only as attachments, with their own allocation, kept with Metal's lossy compression (nvn_mtl.m rt_lossy; about 100 MB at 720p on kid-with-sword). DM_NVN_RT_LOSSY=0 turns it off
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# The game's own 80 % frame scaled up, as on the console, rather than native: smaller 3D targets for a 16 GB Mac (the launcher's Output still offers Native)
# agl wraps its clears in render conditions on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders; the same library here

# The game turns the difference of two raw counter reports into its wind and particle time step at the Switch 2's system counter rate. At NVN's 614.4 MHz the step was 19.66 times too large: foliage, leaves and hanging plants moved about 20 times too fast

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# The game's compute dispatches with no barrier of its between them run side by side (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc): on the kokiri-deck route GPU p50 15.63 -> 14.76 ms (docked,
# Apple M4 Pro, three runs a side), the pictures alike

# The replay's Metal encoding on a thread of its own, as on iOS: the submit thread no longer waits for each pass's encoding, the GPU of a MacBook Air M4 starves less at segment boundaries (frame p50 24.5 → 23.5 ms at 1920x1080 docked, the Hyrule Field view)
